newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 23.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
GUJRAL WINS CONFIDENCE MOTION

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral won the vote of confidence in the lower house of the parliament by a voice vote. Gujral pledged to govern by consensus, bring about national reconciliation and do without political witch hunts. All the political parties, including the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), responded by offering constructive cooperation in his endeavour.
The Economic Times
RELIANCE NET UP BY 180 MLN RUPEES

Reliance Industries (RIL) announced a 13.23 billion rupee net profit for the year ended March 31, 1997. While the net profit was markedly higher than the estimates of 12 billion rupees, it was only marginally above the 13.05 billion profit earned in the previous year. The RIL board also recommended a higher dividend of 65 percent, five percentage points more than the previous year, involving a payout of 2.99 billion rupees, the largest by any company in the private sector. Sales for the year reached 87.3 billion rupees against 77.86 billion in the previous year, an increase of 12 percent.
ITC PARTS WAYS WITH EAGLE STAR

In the first major breakup in the insurance sector, ITC terminated its tieup with Eagle Star Insurance, a subsidiary of its largest shareholder, BAT. ITC and Eagle Star had signed an understanding for an equal joint venture in insurance, including life and general sectors. Financial institution sources quoted ITC officials as saying that the agreement was terminated since it was not a strategic area for the cigarette major. There were indications that ITC may abandon its foray into insurance altogether and concentrate on its core business of tobacco, the sources added.
LEADING INDUSTRY BODY DRAWS AGENDA FOR CORPORATE GOVERNANCE

The corporate governance code, prepared by CII, the leading industry body, has taken into consideration some common shortcomings in management of companies. Exit of financial institutions (FIs) from the management of companies where their shareholdings were less than 10 percent, withdrawal of FI nominees from board of companies not defaulting in loan repayment, removal of restrictions on takeover of companies and debarring defaulting companies from accepting further deposits were some of the major recommendations of the code. The report was likely to form the basis for a policy on corporate governance.
Financial Express
PIVOTALS FAIL TO MAINTAIN INITIAL GAINS ON HECTIC SELLING

Share prices posted modest gains but lost the initial advantage towards the close on heavy selling pressure from speculators at the Bombay bourse (BSE). Reliance Industries was in the limelight following a record profit being posted in its financial results. The prime minister's assurance of continuation of economic reforms irrespective of political uncertainties, reassured the support of foreign institutional investors. The market opened with the BSE sensitive index at 3,813.42 and closed at 3,800.63, showing a gain of 0.84 points from the previous close.
SHIPPING CORP TO ACQUIRE 17 SHIPS FOR $492 MILLION

The Shipping Corporation (SCI) planned to acquire 17 ships, both new and second-hand vessels, in 1997/98 (April-March) at an estimate of over $492 million. Of the vessels to be acquired, eight were planned last financial year. The company bought only one second-hand 29,755 DWT product tanker in 1996/97 for $17 million. SCI would fund the acquisitions by external commercial borrowings (ECBs) and internal accruals, a senior company official said.
INCOME TAX ACT TO BE AMENDED TO ENSURE LEVEL PLAYING FIELD

Sections of the Income Tax Act would be amended to ensure that Unit Trust of India (UTI) and other mutual funds did not face massive outflow of corporate funds because the provision of complete exemption of tax on dividend income was not extended to them. The new Finance Bill exempted dividend incomes of Indian companies from tax. But incomes from UTI and other mutual funds were exempt from tax only to the extent of 15,000 rupees. UTI and other mutual funds had protested to the Finance Ministry against the decision.
Business Standard
COMPLEX FERTILISER PRICES REVISED

The fedral government announced new uniform prices for complex fertilisers for the kharif (summer harvest) season. All state governments were asked to ensure that complex fertilisers were sold at the uniform prices during the season. The maximum retail prices included a freight and distribution margin and were exclusive of local taxes. The central government had announced uniform prices for decontrolled fertilisers on April 1 and issued fresh guidelines for states to monitor these rates.
WORLD BANK FUNDS LIKELY TO ENABLE CUT IN TELECOM RATES

India may be offered World Bank funds to reduce high international telecom rates as a way out of the current row with a U.S.-led Western nations' group. India was resisting pressure from this group to lower tariffs by ending the monopoly of the state-owned carrier, VSNL. An International Telecom Union (ITU) expert group recommended financial and technical help to high telecom tariff countries, to enable them to carry out tariff reduction reforms in line with global trends. The expert group wanted this help to be implemented with the assistance of the World Bank, the World Trade Organisation and ITU.
CENTRAL BANK MOPS UP $50 MLN TO CHECK RUPEE RISE

The Reserve Bank of India bought over $50 million in the foreign exchange market in a bid to arrest the rupee's appreciation against the dollar. The rupee strengthened to 35.74, notching up gains of almost 0.02 rupee overnight. With the RBI limiting its intervention in order to keep within its money supply target, market sources expected the Indian curreny to continue appreciating in the short run.
INMARSAT, DoT IN PACT FOR SATELLITE PHONE SYSTEM

The Department of Telecommunication (DoT) signed a memorandum of understanding with Inmarsat for the latest satellite telephone system for remote area communication. Videsh Sanchar Nigam, the state-owned voice carrier, would provide its gateway and earth stations to enable Inmarsat execute the project. The pilot project would endeavour to study the possibility of using this technology for connecting remote sites of important infrastructural projects.
The Observer
PRUDENTIAL CORP SCOUTING FOR PARTNER

Prudential Corporation, having signed a memorandum of understanding with ICICI, was now scouting for another partner to enter the healthcare business. Prudential proposed to examine other areas apart from the life insurance business, including healthcare, pensions and mutual funds. On account of problems faced in the health insurance segment, with the lack of adequate healthcare delivery system and want of necessary infrastructure, the third partner could be from the healthcare delivery system, a company official indicated.
IBRD FLAYS TARDY EXECUTION OF HIGHWAY PROJECTS

In a highly critical appraisal of the execution of highway projects in India, a World Bank audit mission said implementation of projects funded by it has not only been slow, but even disappointing. The mission also observed that consultants being sent by foreign firms were not of very high calibre. It said foreign joint ventures were in name only with the foreigner lending his name but bringing neither equipment nor finance to India.
